It started with eight young people in Soshanguve.

Some were still in high school, some at tertiary institutions. On 11 September 2009 they met to agree on a name, a vision and a mission. A year later, on 24 September 2010, they launched Agape Youth Movement at a park in Soshanguve Block TT.

Change Starts With Us.
Block TT, 2010

Milestones

The move is on.

  1. 092009

    2009

    Eight young people, one idea

    On 11 September 2009, eight young people in Soshanguve, some in high school and some at tertiary institutions, met to agree on a name, vision and mission. Agape Youth Movement was founded.

  2. 102010

    2010

    Launched in Block TT

    AYM was officially launched on 24 September 2010 at a park in Soshanguve Block TT, drawing a large crowd of young people. It registered as an NPO and ran its first project in Soshanguve.

  3. 112011

    2011

    The Education Pillar

    AYM introduced its Education Pillar and hosted its first Career Expo, “I made it, what about you?”. Career exhibitions in schools, parks and community halls followed. The Agricultural Agape project helped eleven homes plant backyard vegetable gardens (June 2011 – December 2012).

  4. 142014

    2014

    Nine provinces

    The organisation was launched in all nine provinces of South Africa.

  5. 152015

    2015

    First Tshwane Youth Leadership Talk

    The first annual Tshwane Youth Leadership Talk took place on 27 June 2015 at the National Library of South Africa, alongside the launch of the book Beyond Inspiration.

  6. 162016

    2016

    Agape Youth Movement NPC

    AYM registered as a non-profit company (Reg. No. 2016/139118/08).

    ✎ Agape to confirm
    • Confirm registration year and wording.
  7. 172017

    2017

    #Moetapele and new partnerships

    The Department of Basic Education issued a letter of support for #Moetapele (12 April 2017), and AYM signed a three-year strategic partnership with JCI Tshwane.

  8. 182018

    2018

    A five-year partnership with DBE

    A five-year partnership with the Department of Basic Education was established, and Youth Leadership Talks expanded to Durban, Klerksdorp, Polokwane and Johannesburg.

    ✎ Agape to confirm
    • Confirm current status and wording of the DBE partnership/MOU.
  9. 252025

    2025

    RCL Hub goes live

    RCL Hub, the national digital platform for Representative Councils of Learners, launched in June 2025 with the Department of Basic Education, supported by UNICEF, GIZ and AYM.

Archive

Early highlights

From the "Success Stories" page of our previous website, preserved here as part of our history.

  • Since 2010, worked with SANCA and the Truth about Drugs programme to support the rehabilitation of more than 15 young people in Gauteng.
  • Hosted career exhibitions in schools, parks and community halls from 2011.
  • Ran team-building sessions across Gauteng with Spiritual Team Builders.
  • Hosted poetry sessions that gave young writers a platform. Tshepang Sekgororwana was featured in newspapers and Tebogo Motebele appeared on SABC 1.
  • Ran workshops in Pretoria on HIV/AIDS, financial literacy and drug awareness that reached hundreds of young people.

Built by young people. Trusted by institutions.

Agape Youth Movement (AYM) is a youth-led South African non-profit company. It develops learner leaders, strengthens youth participation and builds the tools, both in person and digital, that help schools and government take young people seriously.

Young Voices Matter.

01Vision & mission

Vision and mission

Vision

“A capacitated and empowered youth who take part in the positive transformation of Africa.”

Mission

We design and deliver programmes for young people in townships and rural areas, especially those from previously disadvantaged communities. We use innovative tools to build awareness of their potential, leadership skills and structured support, and we mentor the youth-led organisations that serve them.

Overall goal

Young people who are capacitated and empowered to address their own challenges and those of wider society.

  • 1Build leadership skills among young people, especially in schools.
  • 2Share personal-development information through platforms young people already use.
  • 3With partners, provide peer support and mentorship for youth-led organisations.

02Our values

Six values. Pinned to the wall.

  • Equality

    Every young person's voice carries equal weight.

  • Quality

    Programmes built properly, delivered properly, measured honestly.

  • Inclusiveness

    Open to every young person, regardless of race, sex, ethnicity, culture or ability.

  • Unity

    Ubuntu: we lead with and through each other.

  • Participation

    Young people take part in the decisions about their lives.

  • Transparency

    Open about what we do, what it costs and what it achieves.

AYM's roots are in Christian teachings of agape, or unconditional love. Its programmes are non-religious and non-discriminatory.

03Our approach

How we work.

  1. 01

    Learners at the centre

    We treat learners as the people who define the problem and design the solutions, not as beneficiaries.

  2. 02

    Inside the system

    We work alongside the Department of Basic Education and other public institutions so that what works becomes how things are done.

  3. 03

    Digital where it helps

    Technology like RCL Hub extends the reach of programmes. It doesn't replace the human work of mentorship.

  4. 04

    Evidence and honesty

    We report what we can verify, learn from what didn't work and publish what we learn.

Home / Stories / Between Generations

Podcast · In development

Between Generations.

A podcast where experienced leaders and young South Africans sit at the same table to talk about leadership, the lessons that cost them something, social change and the future they are each building.

This podcast is a concept being developed by Agape Youth Movement and is subject to final approval and launch. No episodes have been released yet.

01Concept & purpose

Two generations. One table.

  • Transfer wisdom

    Lessons from people who have led, failed and led again, told honestly.

  • Challenge assumptions

    Young people push back on the experienced guests and ask the questions others avoid.

  • Build bridges

    Generations that rarely speak directly learn to understand each other.

Announced at launch

Each episode will pair a young host or co-host with an experienced leader from government, business, education, civil society, the arts or sport. We'll profile hosts and guests here once they are confirmed.

01Who we are

Who we are

Eight young people in Soshanguve started Agape in 2009. Today we work with the Department of Basic Education, development partners and schools to make learner leadership work in practice: in workshops, in school governance and on a national digital platform.

Our mission

Programmes that build young people's awareness of their potential, their leadership skills and the structured support around them, especially in townships and rural areas.

Our approach

Learners are at the centre. We work inside public systems and use technology where it helps. Young people are partners, never just an audience.

More about Agape

02What we do

Six ways we move the needle.

What we do

Think. Lead. Act.
  1. Learner Leadership Support

    We train, mentor and resource Representative Councils of Learners so the learners elected to lead can do it well, and we help the education system support them.

  2. Youth Participation & Active Citizenship

    We create structured ways for young people to shape the decisions that affect them, from school governance to national policy dialogues.

  3. Gender-Based Violence Prevention

    Learner-led dialogue, positive masculinity and changemaker training that change norms early, before violence starts.

  4. Online Child Safety

    Awareness, digital literacy and clear routes to help, so children can be safe, smart and kind online.

  5. Capacity Building & Technical Support

    Training, programme design and technical support for government departments, schools and youth-led organisations.

  6. Digital Innovation & Youth Development

    Platforms like RCL Hub that extend our programmes to learner leaders across the country.

We train, mentor and resource Representative Councils of Learners so the learners elected to lead can do it well, and we help the education system support them.

04Innovation in action

Learner leadership, now on every learner's phone.

Innovation in action: RCL Hub

RCL Hub is the national digital platform for Representative Councils of Learners, built with the Department of Basic Education and supported by UNICEF and GIZ. Learner leaders learn their role, run their council and show the difference they make, wherever their school is.

  • Leadership learning
  • Proposals & voting
  • Meetings & tasks
  • Feedback & reporting

03How it will work

From your tool to a learner's hands.

  1. Tell us

    Share your resource, tool or service and who it is for.

  2. We review

    We check fit, safety, child protection, POPIA and quality.

  3. We co-design

    Together we adapt the offer for learner leaders and educators.

  4. Learners use it

    It goes live through Agape channels with a partner profile.

Early Prevention of Gender-Based Violence

School-based and community interventions that promote dignity, equality, positive relationships and violence prevention.

Before it starts

01Why it matters

Prevention works best early, while norms about power, gender and relationships are still forming. Schools reach almost every young person, which makes them the most important place to start.

02How we work on it

  • 1Learner-led dialogue and awareness campaigns.
  • 2Positive Masculinity orientation with boys and young men.
  • 3Sexual and reproductive health education.
  • 4Training changemakers to address bullying and interpersonal violence among peers.

Innovation & Digital Development

Using technology, digital platforms and innovative tools to strengthen youth development.

Tech that extends reach

01Why it matters

South Africa has thousands of public secondary schools, far more than workshops alone can reach. Digital tools let Agape reach more learners while keeping the quality of its in-person work.

02How we work on it

  • 1Building and running RCL Hub with the Department of Basic Education and partners.
  • 2Developing ICT tools that extend the reach and impact of youth work.
  • 3Growing a partner ecosystem of trusted digital resources for learners and educators.

Life Skills

Building practical competencies, social skills, leadership and digital literacy.

Ready for real life

01Why it matters

Exam results only tell part of the story. Young people also need to communicate, solve problems, look after their health, stay safe and plan their futures, and those skills are rarely taught directly.

02How we work on it

  • 1Sport-based learning that opens up conversations about health, safety and equality.
  • 2Public speaking, campaigning and teamwork through changemaker training.
  • 3Health awareness campaigns written in learners' own language, such as the Breast Cancer Awareness Month carousel.

Online Child Safety

Supporting awareness, protection and safer digital environments for children.

Safe, smart, kind online

01Why it matters

Children are online earlier and for longer, often without guidance. Protecting them takes informed children, informed adults and clear pathways to help.

02How we work on it

  • 1Age-appropriate awareness on cyberbullying, grooming, scams and harmful content.
  • 2Digital literacy for learners, parents and educators.
  • 3Designing Agape's own platforms with child-protection and POPIA requirements built in.

Value-Based Leadership

Developing ethical, responsible, empathetic and capable young leaders.

Leadership as responsibility

01Why it matters

A title doesn't make someone a leader. Agape develops leaders whose authority comes from integrity and from serving the people they represent, which is ubuntu put into practice.

02How we work on it

  • 1Leadership curricula built on Agape's values of equality, quality, inclusiveness, unity, participation and transparency.
  • 2Mentorship that follows learners from election through to action.
  • 3Practical projects where leaders solve real problems in their schools.

Youth Participation & Engagement

Young people taking part in the social, educational, community and policy processes that shape their lives.

Seats at the table

01Why it matters

Decisions about schools, safety and opportunity are usually made about young people rather than with them. Representative Councils of Learners exist in law, but the role only works when learners know how to use it and adults make room for them.

02How we work on it

  • 1Strengthening Representative Councils of Learners so learner voice reaches school governance.
  • 2Creating structured spaces such as dialogues, summits and talks where young people engage officials and leaders directly.
  • 3Supporting youth participation in policy work, from consultation to implementation.
  • 4Building digital channels like RCL Hub so participation can happen at scale.

Privacy policy

Last updated: November 2026

✎ Agape to confirm
  • Template text for legal review. Have Agape's legal adviser and Information Officer approve before launch.

1. Who we are

Agape Youth Movement NPC (Reg. No. 2016/139118/08) is the responsible party for personal information collected through this website. Our head office is in Hatfield, Pretoria. Contact our Information Officer at info@aym.org.za.

2. What we collect

Information you give us through forms (name, contact details, organisation, messages, volunteer applications and newsletter subscriptions), and anonymous usage data if analytics is enabled.

3. Why we collect it

To respond to your enquiry, process volunteer applications, send newsletters you asked for, manage partnerships and improve this website. We do not sell personal information.

4. Children

We take particular care with information about learners and children. We publish images of learners only with appropriate consent from parents or guardians and schools, in line with our safeguarding policy. Platforms such as RCL Hub have their own privacy policies.

5. Sharing

We share information only with service providers who help us operate (for example email and form processing), with partners where you have asked us to, or where the law requires.

6. Security & retention

We use reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect information and keep it only as long as needed for the purpose it was collected for.

7. Your rights

Under the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) you may ask to access, correct or delete your information, object to processing, unsubscribe from communications at any time, and lodge a complaint with the Information Regulator.

8. Cookies

This site uses only essential browser storage (for example, remembering that you've seen the intro animation). If analytics is enabled, it is privacy-friendly and does not identify you personally.

Changemakers Network

Grade 9 learners trained to campaign for safer schools.

Active programme

01About the programme

The Changemakers Network gives learners practical knowledge on topics that shape their school day: school safety and the prevention of violence and bullying.

It starts with activation workshops for Grade 9 learners. Selected learners then go through intensive changemaker training, where they learn campaigning and public speaking and how to start change among their peers, especially in addressing interpersonal and gender-based violence.

Trained changemakers join a network of learners in other schools who share ideas and back each other's campaigns.

✎ Agape to confirm
  • Confirm partners, provinces and the network's current engagement model.

Who it serves

  • Grade 9 learners
  • Selected learner changemakers
  • Schools

Areas of work

  • Early Prevention of Gender-Based Violence
  • Youth Participation & Engagement
  • Life Skills

02How it works

The approach.

  1. 1.

    Activation workshops

    Whole-grade sessions that open conversations about safety, violence and bullying.

  2. 2.

    Changemaker training

    Intensive training in campaigning, public speaking and peer leadership for selected learners.

  3. 3.

    Network

    Learner changemakers connect across schools to share campaigns and keep going.

Learner-led GBV Prevention (SR-GBV)

Prevention that starts before violence does, led by learners.

Active programme

01About the programme

Agape's school-related gender-based violence (SR-GBV) prevention work puts learners at the centre. Learners lead the awareness, dialogue and peer conversations that change norms early.

The work promotes dignity, equality and positive relationships. It includes sexual and reproductive health education and Positive Masculinity orientation, which works with boys and young men on what healthy manhood looks like.

✎ Agape to confirm
  • Confirm programme partners, current schools/provinces and any approved results.

Who it serves

  • Learners
  • Boys and young men
  • Educators
  • School communities

Areas of work

  • Early Prevention of Gender-Based Violence
  • Life Skills

02How it works

The approach.

  1. 1.

    Dialogue

    Safe, facilitated conversations that let learners name what they see and experience.

  2. 2.

    Positive masculinity

    Focused sessions with boys and young men on respect, consent and healthy relationships.

  3. 3.

    Learner campaigns

    Learners design and run awareness activities for their own schools.

#Moetapele Learner-Leader Programme

Learner leaders who diagnose their school's problems and design the fixes.

Active programme

01About the programme

#Moetapele (Setswana for 'leader') takes a different approach to poor academic performance, substance abuse, teenage pregnancy and dropout. It treats learners as central to these challenges and to solving them.

It is a three-phase leadership capacity-building programme for RCL members, class leaders and extra-mural leaders. Participants learn to analyse the education challenges in their own school and produce solutions that last after the programme ends.

The Tshwane Youth Leadership Talk, held every year from 2015, raised funds for #Moetapele.

✎ Agape to confirm
  • The old homepage refers to a five-year MOU with DBE. The programme page lists a DBE letter of support dated 12 April 2017. Confirm the current status and approved wording.
  • Confirm whether the three phases are still named See / Design / Lead (labels written for this site).

Who it serves

  • RCL members
  • Class leaders
  • Extra-mural activity leaders
  • Schools

Areas of work

  • Value-Based Leadership
  • Youth Participation & Engagement
  • Life Skills

Partners

Department of Basic Education

02How it works

The approach.

  1. 1.

    Phase 1 — See

    Learner leaders critically analyse the challenges affecting teaching and learning at their school.

  2. 2.

    Phase 2 — Design

    Teams develop practical, school-owned solutions with support from educators.

  3. 3.

    Phase 3 — Lead

    Leaders implement, track and report back on their solutions.

Tshireletso Online Child Safety Initiative

Helping children stay safe, smart and kind online.

Active programme

01About the programme

Tshireletso means 'protection'. The initiative helps children and the adults around them understand the risks children face online, including cyberbullying, grooming, scams and harmful content, and respond to them.

The work combines digital literacy and awareness with knowing where to get help, so children grow up with the confidence to use technology well.

Live since June 2025

RCL Hub. Where learner leaders get to work.

The digital home for South Africa's learner leaders. RCL Hub is the platform Agape built to close that gap. It links leadership development to the everyday work of school governance, so an RCL member can learn the role, act on it and show what changed.

Go to RCL Hub (opens in a new tab)How to get started

Department of Basic Education · UNICEF · German Cooperation (GIZ) · Agape Youth Movement

RCL HubmyRCL

Introduction to an RCL

Leadership learning
Educational resources
Learner participation
Proposals & voting
Meetings
Tasks & responsibilities

01Why RCL Hub

Elected is not the same as equipped.

Young Voices Matter.

Every public secondary school in South Africa must have a functional Representative Council of Learners (RCL). Many learners are elected without ever being shown what the role involves.

RCL Hub is the platform Agape built to close that gap. It links leadership development to the everyday work of school governance, so an RCL member can learn the role, act on it and show what changed.

RCL Hub went live in June 2025. The Department of Basic Education leads it, and UNICEF, German Cooperation (GIZ) through Partnerships for Prevention of Gender-Based Violence in Southern Africa, and Agape Youth Movement support it.

Its wider purpose is to strengthen the role of learner leaders in schools and education structures, giving the education sector a direct, national channel to the learners who represent their peers.

  • Learner participation

    A space for learners to express their views and contribute to school policies.

    Available

  • Proposals & voting

    RCLs table ideas and learners vote on them.

    Available

  • Meetings

    Plan, minute and follow up RCL meetings in one place.

    Available

  • Tasks & responsibilities

    Assign actions to members and track progress.

    Available

  • Feedback & reporting

    Report back to learners, Teacher Liaison Officers and the school.

    Available

  • Recognition & progression

    Learner leaders' growth is recognised as they progress.

    Available

04Who it serves

One platform, six audiences.

  • 01

    Learners

    Understand how the RCL represents you, and use it to raise your voice on school matters.

  • 02

    RCL members

    Learn your role, run meetings, table proposals, track tasks and report back to the learners you represent.

  • 03

    Teacher Liaison Officers

    Guide and support the RCL with shared tools, resources and visibility of its work.

  • 04

    Schools

    A functional RCL that helps build a safe environment for teaching and learning.

  • 05

    District & provincial structures

    See how learner leadership is developing across schools and where support is needed.

  • 06

    Education stakeholders

    A national channel to engage learner leaders on policy, safety and wellbeing.

05How to access it

Three steps in.

  1. 1Go to rcl.org.za on any phone, tablet or computer.
  2. 2Sign in or register with your school details.
  3. 3Start with the 'Introduction to an RCL' lessons, then use the tools with your council.

For learners

For schools

For the education system

A national channel to support and hear from learner leaders across all provinces.

For partners

A trusted route to bring safety, wellbeing and leadership resources to learners.

Ubuntu RCL Leaders Programme

Capacity building and mentorship for learner councils, plus technical support for the education system.

Active programme

01About the programme

The Ubuntu RCL Leaders Programme provides capacity building and mentorship to Representative Councils of Learners. It also gives technical support to the Department of Basic Education at national, provincial and district levels.

The programme starts from ubuntu: a leader is measured by how well the people around them are served. Learner leaders build the skills to represent their peers, take part in school governance and handle conflict responsibly.

  1. 1.

    Train

  2. 2.

    Ongoing mentorship that helps learner leaders put what they have learned into practice at their school.

  3. 3.

    Support the system

    Technical support to DBE structures so learner participation is built into how schools are run.

Youth & Learner Leadership Talks

Dialogues where generations meet to talk leadership.

Ongoing series

01About the programme

The first Tshwane Youth Leadership Talk took place on 27 June 2015 at the National Library of South Africa in Pretoria. The 2016 edition marked the 40th anniversary of the 1976 student uprisings.

From 2018 the talks expanded to Durban, Klerksdorp, Polokwane and Johannesburg. The series now runs as Youth & Learner Leadership Talks, alongside intergenerational dialogues and webinars.

Project highlights1 October 2026

“Hey, can we talk about it?” — a learner-voiced Breast Cancer Awareness Month campaign

A seven-part social carousel that uses school-age characters, myth-busting and a simple Learn–Listen–Support model to open honest health conversations among learners.

ShareWA𝕏

For Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Agape built a campaign around a question learners actually ask: “Hey, why is everyone wearing pink?” Across seven illustrated slides, school-age characters talk through what breast cancer is, what changes to look out for, and who to speak to.

The tone is deliberately peer-to-peer. One slide is a myth-busting challenge: only women get breast cancer, every lump means cancer, talking about it is embarrassing. Each myth is answered with a short, accurate fact. Another slide reminds learners that changes don't always mean cancer but should always be checked by a healthcare professional.

The campaign ends with learner leadership in action, using a three-step model: Learn (share information from reliable sources), Listen (treat people affected by cancer with kindness and respect) and Support (encourage anyone with concerning changes to seek medical advice).

It shows how Agape works on health and life skills. The content is accurate, the language is learners' own, and learner leaders are positioned as the people who make a school a safe place to ask questions.

✎ Agape to confirm
  • Confirm campaign partners and approved description. The slides carry Department of Basic Education and Department of Health identities.

Programme updates30 June 2025

RCL Hub goes live for learner leaders across South Africa

The Department of Basic Education, supported by GIZ and Agape Youth Movement, launched a national online platform for Representative Councils of Learners.

Programme updates
📷 Photo to supply: Featured image for this story
ShareWA𝕏

Related programmes

  • RCL Hub →

Every public secondary school in South Africa is required to have a Representative Council of Learners. Many learners are elected without a clear picture of what the role asks of them. RCL Hub was built to close that gap.

The platform went live in June 2025. The Department of Basic Education leads it with support from GIZ's Partnerships for Prevention programme, UNICEF and Agape Youth Movement. Flow Communications designed and developed the user experience.

Learners can build leadership skills on the platform, find resources on school safety and learner leadership, and take part in shaping their schools. More lessons and resources will be added over time.

“This platform allows the education sector to fast-track the inclusion of learners towards building conducive school environments for teaching and learning,” said Matsetsebale Tleane, Managing Director of AYM.

Source: Flow Communications: Flow helps ignite South Africa's young leaders through the RCL Hub
